The Kastlyra pilot guide

Make the call. Track the signal.

Kastlyra manifesto and pilot guide - Version 0.2 - 23 September 2026

The future is uncertain. Your original view should be clear. What did you expect? How confident were you? What would settle the question? And what happened next?

Kastlyra gives those questions a public record. Inspect a question, choose YES or NO, record your confidence with a Solana wallet, and return to the outcome. No deposits. No wagering. No payouts. The current release is a read-only Solana Devnet pilot while the forecasting program is being reviewed and deployed.

1. The conversation deserves a memory

Market conversation moves quickly. A thoughtful call can disappear between memes and the next headline. We want a better habit: make the question precise, put a view on record before the deadline, and revisit it when the answer becomes knowable. A useful record includes wrong calls, unresolved questions, and cancellations.

2. Three actions, one complete loop

Discover

Browse The board without connecting a wallet. Read the question, closing time, source and resolution rules. If the rules are unclear, do not submit a call.

Commit

Connect Phantom or Solflare and sign a free message to demonstrate wallet control in this browser session. Choose YES or NO and confidence from 50% to 100% for that side. A future Solana program transaction will create the record after deployment. A connection or message signature alone does not create a forecast.

The app never asks for a seed phrase, private key, asset deposit or token approval. Devnet SOL will be needed for fees only after a reviewed program is deployed. The current deployment gate prevents transaction creation.

Reflect

After a question closes, the pilot operator publishes YES, NO or CANCELLED. A future program record will show total calls, resolved calls, correct calls and cancellations. The intended rules are one immutable call per wallet per question and a bounded wallet history.

3. What the pilot currently supports

Available in this release What that means
Public forecast board The interface shows read-only examples while programId is unset.
Solana wallet verification Phantom and Solflare can sign a short-lived message held in page memory.
Deployment gate website/public/deployment.json is deployed: false; no write instruction is available.
Shareable question links Copy a link so someone else can inspect the same question.

The pilot does not include monetary stakes, a trading engine, copy trading, private community workspaces, paid subscriptions, or automated oracle resolution. There is no announced token, airdrop or promise of future rewards. KLYR is a provisional naming placeholder only.

4. A public record is not a trustless answer

A chain can make a submitted record inspectable. It cannot make an ambiguous question precise, prove a person is unique, or guarantee that an operator is correct. The intended resolver is the program authority using the public source and rules stored with each question. Independent review, evidence publication and a dispute path are prerequisites for a mature release.

The Solana program has not been deployed or independently audited. Devnet can reset, data access can fail, and long-term availability is not guaranteed. These limitations are part of the product state, not a hidden assumption.

5. Confidence is a view, not a price

Selecting YES with 70% confidence means you assign 70% probability to YES. Selecting NO with 70% confidence means you assign 70% probability to NO. Neither number is an executable price, investment recommendation or expected return. A board percentage, when live, will represent recorded calls and will not be marketed as a financial market or survey.

7. Where we are headed

Stage Intended work Evidence required
Now: read-only Devnet pilot Clear questions, wallet signing, honest product feedback Reviewed program design and understandable rules
Next: Solana program pilot Deploy markets, forecasts and owner resolution Program tests, deployment record and browser flow
Then: community pilots Recurring rounds, moderator playbooks and evidence recaps Repeat use without financial incentives
Later: portable records Exports, calibration and partner embeds Data quality, privacy controls and demand

These are proposed stages, not announced dates. Mainnet and any token decision require separate technical, security, legal and operational review. Going mainnet would not automatically introduce monetary stakes.

8. Principles

  • Show the original view. Timing, confidence and rules belong beside the result.
  • Keep the full history. Wrong calls and cancellations are part of an honest record.
  • Make room for disagreement. A shared question should not require a shared answer.
  • Explain the limits. A timestamp is evidence of a submission, not proof of truth.
  • Earn the next step. Build useful habits before adding incentives or financial exposure.
